$schema-note: Dated + justified allowlist for the vinext PRE-COMPILE CLOSURE supply-chain gate (scripts/precompile-closure-audit.mjs, ADR-0042 C6 / #764). Mirrors security/npm-audit-allowlist.json and the Trivy triage discipline: an accepted HIGH/CRITICAL in the closure that feeds `vite build` is suppressed ONLY by an entry here, so the gate can never be silently neutered. Each entry MUST carry: `id` (a GHSA/CVE id), `justification` (why it is accepted — no fix available, not reachable in our usage, etc.), `added` (ISO date) and `expires` (strict YYYY-MM-DD, REQUIRED: it must be a real calendar date, i.e. it round-trips; an entry without one makes the gate THROW). Past its expiry the entry stops suppressing and the risk must be re-justified. `note` (free text) and `vendoredIn` (where a vendored copy of the advisory's package lives, for the retirement probe; validated strictly, never suppresses anything) are the only other permitted keys: an entry carrying any key outside [id, justification, added, expires, note, vendoredIn] makes the gate THROW, because a misspelled `expires` would otherwise be silently ignored and the entry would never expire while reading as though it does. A malformed entry makes the gate THROW rather than be ignored. Bump the dependency FIRST (as nanoid 3.3.17 -> 3.3.18 was, via an override in examples/bun-exec/package.json); allowlist only when there is no fix. SCOPE, stated because it is a real widening: this ONE file backs BOTH closures the gate audits — `--closure examples/bun-exec` and `--app apps/file-manager` (C1/#785) — so an entry accepted for one suppresses the same advisory in the other. Every justification must therefore name the closure and the reachability argument it rests on, and an entry whose argument holds only for one closure must be re-examined, not renewed, if the other starts carrying the same package.

allow.justification: decode-uri-component 0.2.2 (quadratic-time DoS in percent-decoding; fixed only in 0.5.1, advisory range <= 0.5.0). Pulled ONLY via query-string@7.1.3 <- minio@8.0.6 <- @getknext/lib (runtime, bundled into the closure). The bump is NOT taken: 0.5.1 is ESM-only (type: module, default export) and query-string 7 require()s it expecting a CJS function, so `query-string.parse` throws `decodeComponent is not a function` (verified under node 24 and bun 1.4.2); minio 8.0.7 (latest) still pins query-string ^7.1.3, so no clean upgrade path exists. REACHABILITY: the decode path is reached only through query-string's parse/extract, and minio's dist calls only `qs.stringify` (internal/client.js, helpers.js) — no request or response bytes are ever decoded by this package. The module is loaded but its quadratic decode routine is never invoked. Applies identically to every closure that carries minio (apps/docs, apps/file-manager, the published @getknext/lib closure). Re-check at expiry: if minio moves to a query-string that pulls a fixed decode-uri-component, or query-string is replaced, bump and drop this entry rather than renewing it; if any code calls query-string.parse on untrusted input, this entry must be dropped and the path fixed. PATCH ROUTE considered and rejected: a bun patchedDependencies edit of query-string 7.1.3 (loading decode-uri-component's `.default`) only changes THIS repo's install; consumers of the published @getknext/lib resolve minio -> query-string -> decode-uri-component themselves, so the published closure would still carry 0.2.2, and the patch would fork a third-party package we then have to maintain.

React Server Components unauthenticated RCE (CRITICAL). REACHABLE: the affected code is the React that next@16.4.3 VENDORS under next/dist/compiled/react-server-dom-{webpack,turbopack} (build 19.3.0-canary/experimental-278794d7-20261002), which serves every RSC request on the default node target in BOTH closures this file backs (apps/file-manager and examples/bun-exec). It is accepted ONLY because there is NO FIX we can apply: no stable Next 16.4.x release vendors a patched React (16.4.5 and 16.4.6 carry the same 20261002 canary), and the vendored copy cannot be overridden by a dependency override. The gate saw this for the first time when it learned to read vendored builds (#61); before that the same exposure existed and scanned as UNKNOWN. The userland copies are outside the affected ranges today, measured on 2026-11-13: in apps/file-manager react-server-dom-webpack and @vitejs/plugin-rsc's vendored copy are 19.3.1, and in examples/bun-exec the top-level react-server-dom-webpack is 19.2.9 (grype: 19.2.9 unaffected, 19.2.8 affected). So this id suppresses only Next's vendored builds today. Short expiry on purpose: re-check weekly for a Next 16.4.x backport, and bump `next` the day one ships.
allow.note: Tracked in #61. Drop this entry, do not renew it, once `next` is pinned to a release whose next/dist/compiled/react-server-dom-* build is 19.3.1+. Because suppression is by advisory id, this entry would also hide a REGRESSION of the userland copies to an affected version — re-read the SUPPRESSED lines in the audit log when renewing.
